dates.title: The dates
dates.text: The 1st round is on Sunday 18 April 2027, the 2nd round on Sunday 2 May.

inscription.title: Register in time
inscription.text: To vote, you must be on the electoral roll by Friday 12 March 2027 at the latest, online or at the town hall. A procuration (proxy vote) has no fixed deadline, but it is best to do it early.

parrainages.title: The 500 parrainages
parrainages.text: To stand as a candidate, you need parrainages (official sponsorships) from 500 elected officials, from at least 30 different départements (French administrative areas).

majorite.title: How you win
majorite.text: A candidate is elected in the 1st round if they get more than half of the votes. If not, only the top two go through to the 2nd round.

melenchon.title: Mélenchon, 4th bid
melenchon.text: Jean-Luc Mélenchon is running for the 4th time, after 2012, 2017 and 2022.

attal.title: Attal, candidate of Macron's party
attal.text: Gabriel Attal took over Emmanuel Macron's party while distancing himself from him, and he is a candidate.

retailleau.title: Retailleau for LR
retailleau.text: Bruno Retailleau, president of Les Républicains (LR), is his party's candidate.

qui-peut-voter.title: Who can vote in France?
qui-peut-voter.text: For the presidential and legislative (parliamentary) elections, you must have French nationality. EU citizens who live in France can vote in municipal and European elections. Other foreign nationals do not vote in political elections.

presidentielle-te-concerne.title: Even if you can't vote, it affects you
presidentielle-te-concerne.text: The president and their government decide policy on visas and residence permits. Since 2019, universities can also charge higher tuition fees to non-EU students.

elections-etudiantes.title: You can vote… in student elections
elections-etudiantes.text: Elections to your university's councils and to the CROUS (student services) are open to all enrolled students, whatever their nationality.

retailleau-rearmer-etat.title: Retailleau wants to "rearm the State" after 17 October
retailleau-rearmer-etat.text: On 18 October, Bruno Retailleau (Les Républicains, LR) accused La France insoumise (LFI) MPs of having "armed violence with their slogans". He proposes a revision of the Constitution to set the age of criminal responsibility for minors at 15 and to introduce minimum sentences.
retailleau-rearmer-etat.why: The proposal concerns how the justice system treats young people under 18.

quiz.question: What age does Bruno Retailleau propose for the criminal responsibility of minors?
quiz.explanation: He proposes a constitutional revision to set it at 15.

mobilisation-17-octobre.title: 17 October: 550,000 protesters against the cost of living
mobilisation-17-octobre.text: On 17 October, about 550,000 people protested across France according to the Interior Ministry (800,000 according to the organisers) against the "high cost of living". Secondary school pupils, students, former gilets jaunes (yellow vests) and trade unions marched; violence and about 400 arrests were reported.
mobilisation-17-octobre.why: Secondary school pupils and students were part of the marches, which focused on the cost of living.

quiz.question: According to the Interior Ministry, how many people protested on 17 October?
quiz.explanation: 800,000 is the organisers' figure; 110,000 is the official figure for Paris only.

ps-motion-rejet-budget.title: Budget: the PS motion to reject is defeated
ps-motion-rejet-budget.text: On 13 October, MPs voted down, by 236 votes to 149, the preliminary motion to reject the 2027 budget tabled by the Parti socialiste (PS). The left supported it; the centre bloc and the Rassemblement national (RN) voted against. So the debate on the bill began.

sides.label: PS (Estelle Mercier)
sides.text: accuses the government of an "absolute taboo: asking the richest to contribute".

sides.label: RN (Sophie-Laurence Roy)
sides.text: accuses the PS of offering the government an opposition that "refuses to discuss".

quiz.question: Which group tabled this motion to reject the budget?
quiz.explanation: The motion came from the socialist MPs; it was rejected by 236 votes to 149.

rn-contre-motion-rejet.title: Budget: the RN refuses to reject the bill outright
rn-contre-motion-rejet.text: On 13 October, the Rassemblement national (RN) MPs, a group chaired by Marine Le Pen, decided to vote against the PS motion to reject the 2027 budget. "Discussing the budget is the basis of Parliament," said Jean-Philippe Tanguy when announcing this choice.

quiz.question: What reason does Jean-Philippe Tanguy give for the RN's vote?
options: The RN supports the government's budget
The RN wants the budget to be debated
quiz.explanation: He said: "We want to have this debate" and "Discussing the budget is the basis of Parliament".

horizons-budget-alternatif.title: Horizons proposes an "alternative budget"
horizons-budget-alternatif.text: Horizons, Édouard Philippe's party, proposes to cancel €10 billion of planned tax rises, offset by the same amount of savings. Among its ideas: reversing the suspension of the pension reform and not replacing one civil servant in three.

quiz.question: How much in tax rises does Horizons want to cancel?
quiz.explanation: Horizons wants to cancel €10 billion of tax rises, offset by €10 billion of savings.

glucksmann-primaire.title: Glucksmann wins the primary in the 1st round
glucksmann-primaire.text: On 11 October, Raphaël Glucksmann (Place publique) won the social democratic primary with 66.17% of the votes, ahead of Olivier Faure (Parti socialiste, PS, 14.46%). He becomes the candidate of the PS, Place publique and the GRS. He said: "There will be no deal with LFI" (La France insoumise).

quiz.question: Who came second in this primary?
quiz.explanation: Olivier Faure, first secretary of the PS, got 14.46%.

melenchon-parcoursup.title: In Clermont, Mélenchon wants to abolish Parcoursup
melenchon-parcoursup.text: At a rally at the Zénith in Clermont-Ferrand on 11 October, Jean-Luc Mélenchon (La France insoumise, LFI) said that "Parcoursup must be abolished" and declared himself opposed to selection at university. He also proposed lowering the voting age to 16.
melenchon-parcoursup.why: Parcoursup is the national platform for admission to higher education after the bac (the secondary school final exam).

quiz.question: At what age does Jean-Luc Mélenchon propose to give the right to vote?
quiz.explanation: He proposed lowering the voting age to 16 (it is 18 today).

attal-pacte-jeunesse.title: Attal presents a "pact for young people"
attal-pacte-jeunesse.text: In Lyon on 10 October, Gabriel Attal (Renaissance) proposed keeping Parcoursup (the higher education admissions platform) but reforming it, with less continuous assessment and more final exams. He also wants fewer pupils per class and a convention of 150 young people aged 16 to 25 chosen by lot.

sides.label: LFI (Jean-Luc Mélenchon)
sides.text: replied on X, denouncing Attal's "appalling duplicity".

quiz.question: What does Gabriel Attal propose for Parcoursup?
quiz.explanation: He wants to keep it, with less continuous assessment and more support.

platret-candidat.title: Gilles Platret declares his candidacy
platret-candidat.text: On 8 October, Gilles Platret, mayor of Chalon-sur-Saône (independent right, formerly LR), made his candidacy official at a public meeting in his town. He proposes abolishing the 35-hour week and restoring national borders. He still has to gather 500 parrainages (official sponsorships from elected officials).
platret-candidat.why: The legal 35-hour working week sets the point from which overtime hours are counted.

quiz.question: What does Gilles Platret propose on working time?
quiz.explanation: He proposes abolishing the legal 35-hour working week.

parcoursup-reforme-gouvernement.title: Parcoursup: the government opens the way to reform
parcoursup-reforme-gouvernement.text: Faced with protests by secondary school pupils, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on 7 October that he wants to "make Parcoursup more transparent and understandable". The Higher Education Minister, Philippe Baptiste, rejects abolishing it but thinks the tool must change.
parcoursup-reforme-gouvernement.why: Parcoursup (the higher education admissions platform) affects the secondary school pupils and students who apply for a course every year.

quiz.question: What is the position of Minister Philippe Baptiste?
quiz.explanation: He opposes abolishing it but says the tool must change.

wauquiez-casseur-payeur.title: Wauquiez wants vandals to pay
wauquiez-casseur-payeur.text: On 2 October, Laurent Wauquiez, leader of the Les Républicains (LR) MPs, asked that people who cause damage during secondary school protests pay for the repairs: "you break it, you pay". This principle has been in the law since 2019, but préfectures (the State's local offices) do not use it, according to the government.

quiz.question: Since when has the "you break it, you pay" principle been in the law?
quiz.explanation: It has been in force since 2019, but in practice the préfectures do not apply it.

budget-2027-education-apl.title: 2027 budget: APL frozen, more money for schools
budget-2027-education-apl.text: The 2027 draft budget plans €65.53 billion for school education (64.43 in 2026) and €500 million more for higher education. The APL (housing benefit) would not be raised, and well-off households would have to choose between their student child's APL and the extra tax allowance (demi-part fiscale).
budget-2027-education-apl.why: Many students who rent receive the APL; these measures are still being debated in Parliament.

quiz.question: What does the draft budget plan for the APL in 2027?
quiz.explanation: The APL would not be raised next year; only well-off households would have to choose between the APL and the demi-part.

philippe-retraites-65-ans.title: Philippe proposes retirement at 65
philippe-retraites-65-ans.text: On 29 September, Édouard Philippe (Horizons) presented his plan: relaunch the 2023 reform, then within less than ten years raise the legal retirement age to 65 and the contribution period to 45 years. He wants to add a funded (capitalisation) component to the pay-as-you-go system.
philippe-retraites-65-ans.why: The contribution period would apply to people starting their working life today.

quiz.question: What contribution period does Édouard Philippe propose?
quiz.explanation: He proposes 45 years of contributions and a legal age of 65, reached in less than ten years.

rn-groupe-senat.title: Senate elections: the RN can form a group in the Senate
rn-groupe-senat.text: In the Senate elections of 27 September, the Rassemblement national (RN) and its allies got 12 new senators elected, when they had only 3. They pass the threshold of 10 members needed to form a group, a first for them in the history of the Senate.
rn-groupe-senat.why: The Senate votes on laws, including the budget, together with the Assemblée nationale (National Assembly).

quiz.question: What is the minimum number of senators needed to form a group in the Senate?
quiz.explanation: The threshold is ten members of parliament; the RN and its allies passed it.

becht-extreme-centre.title: Olivier Becht, candidate of the "extreme centre"
becht-extreme-centre.text: On 24 September, in Paris Match, Olivier Becht, MP for the Haut-Rhin and former Minister Delegate for Foreign Trade, announced his candidacy. He calls himself "in the extreme centre" and presents a plan called "Le Projet France, Refonder ou Périr" ("The France Project: Rebuild or Perish").

quiz.question: Which ministerial post did Olivier Becht hold?
quiz.explanation: He was Minister Delegate for Foreign Trade from 2022 to January 2024.

macron-taxes-carburants.title: Macron does not rule out cutting fuel taxes
macron-taxes-carburants.text: Asked on France 2 and TF1 on 24 September, Emmanuel Macron did not rule out cutting fuel taxes if prices keep rising, while saying it is "not the most virtuous decision", because these taxes fund State spending.

sides.label: RN (Sébastien Chenu)
sides.text: "Emmanuel Macron is out of touch when he says he doesn't want to cut fuel taxes".

sides.label: LR (François-Xavier Bellamy)
sides.text: "there are levers for action, we are not condemned to doing nothing".

sides.label: LFI (Éric Coquerel)
sides.text: "the head of State is showing himself to be powerless".

ecologistes-vote-decembre.title: Les Écologistes: Tondelier is a candidate, final choice in December
ecologistes-vote-decembre.text: On 21 September, the federal council of Les Écologistes (the Greens) adopted, with 69.44%, a motion that drops the plan for a primary. Marine Tondelier remains a candidate until the members' vote (10-13 December), when they will choose between a Green candidacy and supporting another left-wing candidate.

quiz.question: What will Green party members decide from 10 to 13 December?
options: Whether they keep their candidate or support another left-wing candidate
The name of their Prime Minister
quiz.explanation: They will choose between a candidacy from their party and supporting a candidate from another left-wing force.

repas-1-euro-budget.title: €1 meals: €143 million planned in the 2027 budget
repas-1-euro-budget.text: Since 4 May 2026, all students can eat at the university restaurant for €1, with no means test. The government plans €143 million for this scheme in 2027 and warns that it could not be guaranteed for everyone unless the budget is adopted.
repas-1-euro-budget.why: The price of a meal at the university restaurant has gone from €3.30 to €1 for all students.

quiz.question: Since when has the €1 meal been open to all students?
quiz.explanation: Before 4 May 2026, it was reserved for grant holders and students in financial hardship.

rn-bardella-seul-candidat.title: RN: Bardella is the only candidate for re-election
rn-bardella-seul-candidat.text: More than 112,000 members of the Rassemblement national (RN) are invited to vote online until 22 October to elect the party president, ahead of a congress in Orléans at the end of October. Jordan Bardella is the only candidate; members can also cast a blank vote, and they elect 100 members of the national council.

quiz.question: Until when can RN members vote?
quiz.explanation: The online vote is open until 22 October inclusive.

zemmour-candidat.title: Éric Zemmour confirms his candidacy
zemmour-candidat.text: On 17 September on BFMTV, Éric Zemmour, president of Reconquête, confirmed that he will be a candidate in the 2027 presidential election. He came fourth in the first round in 2022, with 7.07% of the votes. He announced that he will campaign with Sarah Knafo.

quiz.question: What score did Éric Zemmour get in the 1st round in 2022?
quiz.explanation: He got 7.07% and came fourth.

budget-2027-effort-54-milliards.title: 2027 budget: a €54 billion effort announced
budget-2027-effort-54-milliards.text: On 17 September, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu presented a budget effort of about €54 billion for 2027. The goal: a public deficit of 5% of GDP (4.8% excluding new military spending). The point d'indice (the base for civil servants' pay) would be frozen.
budget-2027-effort-54-milliards.why: The budget sets the funding for universities, student grants and housing benefits.

quiz.question: What public deficit is the government aiming for in 2027?
quiz.explanation: The target is 5% of GDP; without savings, the deficit would be close to 6.5%.

retailleau-refuse-rassemblement.title: Retailleau rejects an alliance with Philippe
retailleau-refuse-rassemblement.text: On 16 September on franceinfo, Bruno Retailleau (Les Républicains, LR) rejected the idea of uniting the right and the centre for 2027. His difference with Édouard Philippe is "not just one of degree, but of nature", he said: "This presidential election will not be won in the centre".

roussel-taxes-essence.title: Roussel calls for lower taxes on petrol
roussel-taxes-essence.text: At the Fête de l'Humanité on 12 September, Fabien Roussel (Parti communiste français, PCF) called for "lower taxes on petrol" and higher wages and pensions. He proposed a "sanction nationalisation" of TotalEnergies and called on people to "invade the roundabouts".

quiz.question: Which company does Fabien Roussel propose to nationalise?
quiz.explanation: He proposed a "sanction nationalisation" of TotalEnergies.

parrainages-500.title: Presidential election: the 500 parrainages rule
parrainages-500.text: To stand, a candidate must gather at least 500 parrainages (official sponsorships from elected officials) from at least 30 départements or overseas territories, with no more than 50 per territory. An elected official can sponsor only one candidate. The official collection period is due to end on 12 March 2027.

quiz.question: What is the minimum number of parrainages from elected officials needed to be a candidate?
quiz.explanation: You need 500 parrainages, from at least 30 départements or overseas territories.

q-duree-mandat.question: For how long is the President of the Republic elected?
q-duree-mandat.explanation: The president is elected for five years by direct universal suffrage, and no one can serve more than two consecutive terms.

q-second-tour.question: Who can stand in the second round of the presidential election?
options: All candidates with more than 12.5% of the votes
q-second-tour.explanation: Only the two candidates who came top in the 1st round (after any withdrawals) can stand in the second round.

q-premier-ministre.question: Who appoints the Prime Minister?
q-premier-ministre.explanation: The President of the Republic appoints the Prime Minister (Article 8 of the Constitution).

q-inscription.question: Until when can you register on the electoral roll for the presidential election?
q-inscription.explanation: You must be registered by Friday 12 March 2027 at the latest, online or at the town hall. A procuration (proxy vote), on the other hand, has no fixed deadline: best to do it early.

q-parrainages.question: What is the minimum number of parrainages (sponsorships from elected officials) needed to be a candidate?
q-parrainages.explanation: You need at least 500 signatures from elected officials, from at least 30 different départements or overseas territories.

q-primaire.question: Who won the social democratic left's primary?
q-primaire.explanation: Raphaël Glucksmann won in the 1st round, on 11 October 2026, with 66.17% of the votes (14.46% for Olivier Faure).

q-age-candidat.question: What is the minimum age to be a candidate in the presidential election?
q-age-candidat.explanation: You must be at least 18. Until an organic law in 2011, you had to be 23.

q-proclamation.question: Who announces the official results of the presidential election?
q-proclamation.explanation: The Conseil constitutionnel announces the official results; for the second round, by 12 May 2027 at the latest.

q-delai-tours.question: How much time is there between the two rounds of the presidential election?
q-delai-tours.explanation: The second round takes place on the fourteenth day after the first: 2 May 2027, two weeks after 18 April.

vf-dates.statement: The 1st round of the presidential election will be held on Sunday 18 April 2027.
vf-dates.explanation: The 1st round is set for Sunday 18 April and the 2nd round for Sunday 2 May 2027.

vf-inscription.statement: You can register on the electoral roll up to the day before the vote.
vf-inscription.explanation: You must be registered by Friday 12 March 2027 at the latest, the 6th Friday before the vote. A procuration (proxy vote), on the other hand, has no fixed deadline: best to do it early.

vf-majorite.statement: A candidate who gets more than 50% of the valid votes in the 1st round is elected without a second round.
vf-majorite.explanation: The president is elected by an absolute majority of the valid votes. If no one gets it, the top two candidates face each other in the second round.

vf-macron-mandat.statement: Emmanuel Macron can run again in 2027.
vf-macron-mandat.explanation: Since 2008, the Constitution says that "no one may serve more than two consecutive terms". Emmanuel Macron is finishing his 2nd term: he cannot be a candidate in 2027.

vf-melenchon.statement: Jean-Luc Mélenchon is running in the presidential election for the first time.
vf-melenchon.explanation: It is his 4th bid, after 2012, 2017 and 2022 (21.95% in the 1st round in 2022).

vf-attal.statement: Gabriel Attal is the candidate of Les Républicains (LR).
vf-attal.explanation: Gabriel Attal is the candidate for Renaissance, which he has led since December 2024. The LR candidate is Bruno Retailleau, chosen by party members in April 2026.

vf-parrainages.statement: To be a candidate, you need at least 500 signatures from elected officials from at least 30 départements or overseas territories.
vf-parrainages.explanation: These are the "parrainages" (official sponsorships). They must reach the Conseil constitutionnel (Constitutional Council) by 6 pm on 12 March 2027 at the latest, and an elected official can sponsor only one candidate.

vf-glucksmann.statement: Raphaël Glucksmann won the social democratic left's primary with about 66% of the votes.
vf-glucksmann.explanation: He won in the 1st round, on 11 October 2026, with 66.17% of the votes, far ahead of Olivier Faure (14.46%).

vf-dissolution-senat.statement: The President of the Republic can dissolve the Senate.
vf-dissolution-senat.explanation: The president can dissolve the Assemblée nationale (National Assembly), after consulting the Prime Minister and the presidents of both chambers, but not the Senate.

vf-parlement-loi.statement: In France, it is Parliament, not the President of the Republic, that votes on laws.
vf-parlement-loi.explanation: Article 24 of the Constitution says: "Parliament shall pass statutes." Parliament is made up of the Assemblée nationale and the Senate.

vf-repas-1-euro.statement: The €1 meal at the university restaurant is only for students with a grant.
vf-repas-1-euro.explanation: Since 4 May 2026, it has been open to all students, with no means test. Before, it was reserved for grant holders and students in financial hardship.

vf-le-pen-candidate.statement: After her conviction on appeal on 7 July 2026, Marine Le Pen confirmed that she would be a candidate in 2027.
vf-le-pen-candidate.explanation: Among other penalties, the appeal court gave her 15 months of ineligibility with immediate effect, which makes her candidacy "theoretically possible". She confirmed it the same day.

vf-abstention.statement: In 2022, more than 6 in 10 young people aged 18-24 did not vote in the 1st round of the presidential election.
vf-abstention.explanation: According to Ipsos/Sopra Steria, about 42% of 18-24 year olds abstained, which is 4 in 10. Abstention among all registered voters was 26.31%.

vf-interim.statement: If the president leaves office before the end of their term, the Prime Minister replaces them until the next election.
vf-interim.explanation: It is the President of the Senate who acts as interim president. Among other limits, they cannot dissolve the Assemblée nationale or call a referendum.

vf-procuration-commune.statement: You can give a procuration (proxy vote) to someone registered in a different commune (municipality) from yours.
vf-procuration-commune.explanation: You can choose any voter; they will vote for you at your polling station, not theirs.

vf-retailleau-1er-mai.statement: Bruno Retailleau criticised the choice of 2 May 2027, the day after 1 May (Labour Day), for the second round.
vf-retailleau-1er-mai.explanation: On 1 July 2026, he said he was "angry" about dates that were "not neutral", fearing the political impact of the 1 May marches.

qp-melenchon-parcoursup.explanation: It was Jean-Luc Mélenchon (La France insoumise, LFI), at his rally at the Zénith in Clermont-Ferrand on 11 October 2026. Parcoursup is the higher education admissions platform.

qp-glucksmann-lfi.prompt: "If I win, there will never again be a deal with Jean-Luc Mélenchon"
qp-glucksmann-lfi.explanation: It was Raphaël Glucksmann (Place publique), announcing his candidacy on the TF1 evening news on 23 August 2026.

qp-roussel-total.prompt: A "sanction nationalisation" of TotalEnergies and "lower taxes on petrol"
qp-roussel-total.explanation: It was Fabien Roussel, candidate of the Parti communiste français (PCF), at the Fête de l'Humanité on 12 September 2026.

qp-philippe-retraites.prompt: Move, within less than ten years, to a legal retirement age of 65 and 45 years of contributions
qp-philippe-retraites.explanation: It was Édouard Philippe (Horizons), who presented this pension reform plan on 29 September 2026.

qp-attal-controle-continu.prompt: Change Parcoursup and reduce "the pressure of continuous assessment" in favour of more final exams
qp-attal-controle-continu.explanation: It was Gabriel Attal (Renaissance), at his rally in Lyon on 10 October 2026.

qp-attal-convention.prompt: Choose 150 young people aged 16 to 25 by lot to take part in "a convention on our proposals"
qp-attal-convention.explanation: It was Gabriel Attal (Renaissance), in his plan for young people presented in Lyon on 10 October 2026.

qp-retailleau-majorite-penale.prompt: Revise the Constitution so that "the age of criminal responsibility for minors is 15" and introduce minimum sentences
qp-retailleau-majorite-penale.explanation: It was Bruno Retailleau, president and candidate of Les Républicains (LR), on France Inter and France 2 on 18 October 2026.

qp-wauquiez-casseur-payeur.prompt: "You break it, you pay": make people who cause damage during secondary school protests pay
qp-wauquiez-casseur-payeur.explanation: It was Laurent Wauquiez, leader of the LR MPs, on 2 October 2026; this principle has been in the law since 2019.

qp-retailleau-centre.prompt: "This presidential election will not be won in the centre"
qp-retailleau-centre.explanation: It was Bruno Retailleau (LR), on franceinfo on 16 September 2026, rejecting an alliance with Édouard Philippe.

qp-lepen-logement.prompt: Give "priority access to social housing to French people" and repeal the loi SRU (the law requiring towns to have a share of social housing)
qp-lepen-logement.explanation: It was Marine Le Pen (Rassemblement national, RN), in her back-to-school speech in Hénin-Beaumont on 13 September 2026.

qp-zemmour-chomage.prompt: Expel a foreign national, "even one legally resident", after one year of unemployment
qp-zemmour-chomage.explanation: It was Éric Zemmour (Reconquête), on BFMTV on 17 September 2026, confirming his candidacy.

qp-lepen-contre-budget.prompt: A counter-budget with "€140 billion of savings by 2032"
qp-lepen-contre-budget.explanation: It was Marine Le Pen (RN), who presented her party's counter-budget on 6 October 2026; about 20% of these savings would come from immigration.

autre-camp.resultMessage: Understanding the other side's arguments does not mean agreeing with them. It makes debate possible.

ac-35h.pour: Working more would mean producing more and raising wages.
ac-35h.contre: The 35-hour week helps share out work and protects personal life.
ac-35h.offTopicCorrection: False: the 35-hour week comes from the Aubry laws of 1998 and 2000.

ac-smic.topic: Raise the SMIC (national minimum wage) sharply
ac-smic.pour: It directly helps the purchasing power of the lowest-paid workers.
ac-smic.contre: It raises labour costs and can slow hiring in small businesses.
ac-smic.offTopic: The SMIC is set by each company.
ac-smic.offTopicCorrection: False: the SMIC is set nationally by the State.

ac-tva.topic: Cut TVA (VAT, sales tax) on essential goods
ac-tva.pour: Prices go down straight away at the till for everyone.
ac-tva.contre: It costs the State a lot and shops do not always lower their prices.
ac-tva.offTopic: TVA does not apply to food.
ac-tva.offTopicCorrection: False: food is subject to TVA, usually at the reduced rate of 5.5%.

p-candidats.question: How many candidates will get their 500 parrainages (sponsorships from elected officials)?

p-participation.question: Turnout in the 1st round will be…
p-participation.context: In 2022, about 74% of registered voters voted in the 1st round.

p-abstention-jeunes.question: Abstention among 18-24 year olds in the 1st round will be…
p-abstention-jeunes.context: In 2022, about 41% of 18-24 year olds did not vote in the 1st round.

maisons.name: The houses
maisons.title: Housing
facts: The commune (municipality) issues building permits and sets planning rules.
The State sets the rules for renting and housing benefits, such as the APL (housing benefit), paid by the CAF (family benefits office).
maisons.forYou: If you rent a home, you may be able to get the APL: run a simulation on the CAF website.

mairie.name: The town hall
mairie.title: The town hall
facts: The municipal council is elected for 6 years, then it elects the mayor. The last municipal elections were held in March 2026.
The town hall handles civil registration (births, marriages, deaths), nursery and primary schools, planning and the electoral roll.
mairie.forYou: You register on the electoral roll at the town hall, or online at service-public.fr. Deadline for the presidential election: Friday 12 March 2027.

ecole.name: The school
ecole.title: Who runs schools?
facts: Nursery and primary school buildings are the responsibility of the commune, collèges (lower secondary schools) of the département, and lycées (upper secondary schools) of the région.
Curricula and teachers depend on the State (Éducation nationale, the national education system). Universities and student grants are also the State's responsibility.
ecole.forYou: Means-tested grants (bourses sur critères sociaux) are applied for every year through the dossier social étudiant (student social file), on messervices.etudiant.gouv.fr.

bibliotheque.name: The library
bibliotheque.title: The library
facts: Most public libraries are run by communes or intercommunalités (groups of municipalities).
Their budget is voted by the municipal or community council.
bibliotheque.forYou: Ask your town's library: many offer reduced rates for students.

parc.name: The park
parc.title: Green spaces
facts: Public parks and gardens are usually run by the commune.
The 2021 Climate and Resilience Law sets a goal of "zero net land take" (zéro artificialisation nette) by 2050.
parc.forYou: Building housing or keeping natural spaces: this is one of the choices local elected officials make.

tram.name: The tram
tram.title: Transport
facts: Urban transport is organised by a mobility authority, often the intercommunalité (group of municipalities).
Régions organise the TER (regional trains). In Île-de-France, it is Île-de-France Mobilités, chaired by the president of the région.
tram.forYou: The price of your transport pass is decided locally, not by the President of the Republic.

stade.name: The stadium
stade.title: Sport
facts: Sports facilities are most often built and run by communes and intercommunalités.
The Ministry of Sport sets national sports policy.
stade.forYou: Sports halls, swimming pools, pitches: their opening hours and prices are often decided locally.

assemblee.name: The Assembly
assemblee.title: The Assemblée nationale (National Assembly)
facts: 577 députés (MPs) are elected for 5 years by direct universal suffrage.
Together with the Senate, the Assembly votes on laws and the budget. It scrutinises the government and can bring it down with a motion de censure (no-confidence motion).
assemblee.forYou: The president is elected in 2027, but needs a majority in the Assembly to get their plans voted through.

france.label: French, living in France
france.summary: You must be on the electoral roll by Friday 12 March 2027 at the latest. Then you vote in person or by proxy (procuration).

etranger.label: French, living abroad
etranger.summary: You can vote at the consulate of your country of residence, or stay registered in a town in France. Either way, register before Friday 12 March 2027.

ue.label: EU citizen in France
ue.summary: The presidential election is for French citizens only. In France, you can vote in municipal and European elections, and in student elections.

hors-ue.label: Non-EU citizen in France
hors-ue.summary: Political elections in France are for French citizens (and EU citizens for municipal and European elections). But you can vote in student elections.

inscription.title: Register on the electoral roll
inscription.intro: No registration, no vote. For the presidential election, the deadline is Friday 12 March 2027, online or at the town hall.

steps.text: Check whether you are already registered and where you vote. If you did your census (recensement citoyen) at 16, you were registered automatically at 18.

link.label: Check my registration and polling station

steps.text: Not registered? Pick your town: where you live, where you have lived for at least 6 months, or where you have paid local taxes for at least 2 years.
Register online with an ID and a proof of address less than 3 months old. Or go to the town hall (mairie) with form cerfa no. 12669.

inscription.tip: Since 1 July 2026, the deadline is the same online and at the town hall: the 6th Friday before the vote.

etudiant.title: Studying far from home?
etudiant.intro: You can vote where you study or stay registered at your parents'.

steps.text: Pick your voting town: where you live for your studies (your home, or for at least 6 months), or your parents' town if you are under 26.
Staying registered far from where you study? Check whether you can go back on 18 April and 2 May 2027. If not, plan a proxy vote (see below).

jour-du-vote.title: Election day
jour-du-vote.intro: Polling stations are open from 8am to 7pm, sometimes up to 8pm at most in some cities. You vote in person or by proxy: there is no online voting.

steps.text: Find your polling station: it is on your voter card and on the registration check service.

Bring an original photo ID: ID card or passport (valid or expired less than 5 years ago), or a valid driving licence, carte Vitale with photo… It is required in towns of 1,000 inhabitants or more. A student card, a photo or a download on your phone are not accepted.
Take an envelope and at least 2 ballots, go into the voting booth (isoloir), put the envelope in the ballot box yourself, then sign the voter list (liste d'émargement).

jour-du-vote.tip: Your voter card is not required to vote. A blank vote counts among voters, but not among valid votes cast (suffrages exprimés).

procuration.title: Can't make it? Vote by proxy
procuration.intro: A voter of your choice votes for you, at your polling station. They can be registered in another town.

steps.text: Ask the person you chose for their date of birth and their national voter number (numéro national d'électeur), which they can find on the registration check service.
Make your request online on Maprocuration, logging in with FranceConnect.

Then go in person to a police or gendarmerie station (a consulate or embassy if you live abroad) with your ID and your request reference. With a certified France Identité digital identity, everything can be done online.
Wait for the confirmation email: your proxy is then valid. Tell the person you chose.

procuration.tip: There is no fixed deadline, but do it as early as possible. You can give it for one round, both rounds, or for up to 1 year. One person can hold only one proxy made in France.

etranger.title: Voting from abroad
etranger.intro: Two options for the presidential election: vote at the consulate (consular electoral roll) or stay registered in a town in France. You can't be on both lists.

steps.text: Choose your list. Consular: you vote in your country of residence. Town in France: you vote in France, in person or by proxy (handy for Erasmus or an internship of a few months).
For the consular roll, register online on the Register of French citizens abroad, or at the consulate, by the 6th Friday before the vote at the latest (Friday 12 March 2027).
On the day, vote in person at the embassy or consulate polling station with an ID, or give a proxy (see below).

etranger.tip: No online or postal voting for the presidential election: online voting only exists for the legislative elections of French citizens abroad and consular elections. In the Americas, voting usually takes place on the Saturday (as in 2022): check the date with your consulate.

ue.title: Municipal and European elections
ue.intro: As a citizen of another EU country living in France, you can vote in municipal and European elections.

steps.text: Register on your town's complementary electoral rolls (listes complémentaires): online, at the town hall or by post, with your ID card, passport or residence permit, a proof of address and a written declaration.
Do it by the 6th Friday before the 1st round of the election you want to vote in.
For European elections, choose: vote in France or in your home country. Not both.

ue.tip: You can also stand in municipal elections, but you can't become mayor or deputy mayor.

hors-ue.title: Student elections
hors-ue.intro: Whatever your nationality, you can vote for your student representatives.

steps.text: Vote in your university council elections: international students can vote and stand on the same terms as French students.
Vote for the student representatives at the CROUS (housing, university restaurants, grants): every student is invited to vote.
Does your country let its citizens abroad vote? Ask your embassy or consulate.

hors-ue.tip: Even if you can't vote, the presidential election affects you: the government decides, for example, visa and residence permit policy.

vote-des-femmes-1944.title: Women win the right to vote
vote-des-femmes-1944.text: The ordinance of 21 April 1944 makes women "voters and eligible under the same conditions as men". They vote for the first time in the municipal elections of 29 April 1945.
vote-des-femmes-1944.why: Truly universal suffrage is recent: in 2027, women and men vote and stand for office on equal terms.

constitution-1958.title: The Fifth Republic's Constitution
constitution-1958.text: Approved by referendum on 28 September 1958 by 79.25% of voters, the new Constitution is proclaimed on 4 October 1958. It strengthens the executive relative to Parliament.
constitution-1958.why: It is still the Constitution in force: it sets the powers of the president elected in 2027, the government and Parliament.

referendum-election-directe-1962.title: President to be elected directly by citizens
referendum-election-directe-1962.text: In a referendum, 62.25% of votes cast approve electing the President of the Republic by direct universal suffrage. Until then, the president was chosen by an electoral college of officials.
referendum-election-directe-1962.why: This is why in 2027 every voter directly chooses the president, making it the central election.

premiere-presidentielle-directe-1965.title: First direct presidential election
premiere-presidentielle-directe-1965.text: In the first round on 5 December 1965, General de Gaulle fails to win an absolute majority and is forced into a run-off. He is elected in the second round on 19 December against François Mitterrand.
premiere-presidentielle-directe-1965.why: It shows the two-round rule: without an absolute majority in round one, only the top two candidates face off in round two.

vote-a-18-ans-1974.title: Voting age lowered to 18
vote-a-18-ans-1974.text: The law of 5 July 1974 lowers the age of majority, and therefore the voting age, from 21 to 18. Millions of young people become voters.
vote-a-18-ans-1974.why: Any French citizen who is 18 by the day before the vote can vote in 2027.

alternance-1981.title: First change of political side in power
alternance-1981.text: François Mitterrand (Socialist Party) is elected with about 51.76% of votes cast against outgoing president Valéry Giscard d'Estaing. He is the Fifth Republic's first left-wing president.
alternance-1981.why: It shows the institutions allow power to pass peacefully from one political side to another through elections.

premiere-cohabitation-1986.title: The first "cohabitation"
premiere-cohabitation-1986.text: After the March 1986 legislative elections, won by the right-wing opposition, Socialist president François Mitterrand appoints Jacques Chirac Prime Minister. The president and the Assembly majority are from opposing camps.
premiere-cohabitation-1986.why: If the president elected in 2027 lacks a majority in the legislative elections, they may have to govern with a Prime Minister from another camp.

referendum-quinquennat-2000.title: Five-year term replaces seven-year term
referendum-quinquennat-2000.text: In a referendum, 73% of votes cast approve cutting the presidential term from seven to five years, with record abstention of about 70% of registered voters.
referendum-quinquennat-2000.why: This is why the president is elected every five years: after 2022, the next election is in 2027.

inversion-calendrier-2001.title: Presidential election moved before legislative
inversion-calendrier-2001.text: An organic law changes the end date of the term of deputies elected in 1997. As a result, from 2002 the presidential election takes place a few weeks before the legislative elections.
inversion-calendrier-2001.why: This is why legislative elections normally follow the presidential one, to give the new president a majority.

21-avril-2002.title: 21 April 2002
21-avril-2002.text: Jean-Marie Le Pen (Front national) reaches the second round and Socialist candidate Lionel Jospin is eliminated. Jacques Chirac is re-elected on 5 May with 82.21% of votes cast.
21-avril-2002.why: It shows that scattered first-round votes can change who reaches the run-off, an issue debated before every presidential election.

revision-constitutionnelle-2008.title: 2008 constitutional reform
revision-constitutionnelle-2008.text: The constitutional law of 23 July 2008 limits the president to two consecutive terms and restricts Article 49.3 to budget bills plus one other text per session. It also creates the priority question of constitutionality.
revision-constitutionnelle-2008.why: Emmanuel Macron, elected in 2017 and re-elected in 2022, cannot run in 2027: no one may serve more than two consecutive terms.

election-macron-2017.title: A president from outside traditional parties
election-macron-2017.text: Emmanuel Macron, founder of the En Marche! movement, is elected against Marine Le Pen with about 66.10% of votes cast. No Socialist or Republican candidate reaches the second round.
election-macron-2017.why: This election reshaped the political landscape: in 2027, the choice is no longer the old left-right face-off.

majorite-relative-2022.title: Only a relative majority
majorite-relative-2022.text: In the legislative elections after Emmanuel Macron's re-election, his Ensemble coalition wins 246 seats, short of the 289 absolute majority. No group can pass laws on its own.
majorite-relative-2022.why: Without an absolute majority, a government must negotiate or use Article 49.3 and faces censure motions, as since 2022.

retraites-49-3-2023.title: Pension reform passed with Article 49.3
retraites-49-3-2023.text: Prime Minister Élisabeth Borne invokes Article 49.3 on the reform raising the legal retirement age to 64. On 20 March, the main censure motion fails by 9 votes.
retraites-49-3-2023.why: Pensions and the use of Article 49.3 remain major issues of political debate ahead of 2027.

dissolution-2024.title: Dissolution of the National Assembly
dissolution-2024.text: On the evening of the European elections, Emmanuel Macron dissolves the National Assembly. Early legislative elections take place on 30 June and 7 July 2024.
dissolution-2024.why: The fragmented Assembly elected in 2024 explains the government instability preceding the 2027 presidential election.

censure-barnier-2024.title: Barnier government brought down
censure-barnier-2024.text: After Article 49.3 is used on the social security budget, a censure motion is passed by 331 deputies. It is only the second time a Fifth Republic government is censured, after 1962.
censure-barnier-2024.why: It shows the Assembly can bring down the government, a key check on executive power in an Assembly without a majority.

confiance-bayrou-2025.title: Bayrou government loses confidence vote
confiance-bayrou-2025.text: Prime Minister François Bayrou asks the National Assembly for a vote of confidence: 364 deputies vote against, 194 in favour. The government must resign.
confiance-bayrou-2025.why: Three Prime Ministers in about a year: securing a stable majority will be a central question after 2027.

budget-2026-49-3.title: 2026 budget passed after Article 49.3
budget-2026-49-3.text: Sébastien Lecornu's government uses Article 49.3 on the 2026 State budget. On 2 February 2026, the last two censure motions are rejected (260 votes at most, 289 needed): the budget is adopted.
budget-2026-49-3.why: The 2027 budget, debated in autumn 2026, is fought in the same Assembly with the same tools: Article 49.3 and censure motions.

debat-1974.title: 1974: the very first runoff debate
debat-1974.text: On 10 May 1974, Valéry Giscard d'Estaing and François Mitterrand debated for about 90 minutes on both public channels, a first in France. Moderated by Jacqueline Baudrier and Alain Duhamel, it focused on economic growth and social justice.
debat-1974.why: It started a tradition: since 1974, a televised duel has preceded the runoff of every presidential election except 2002.
debat-1974.quote: You do not, Mr Mitterrand, have a monopoly on heart.
debat-1974.result: Valéry Giscard d'Estaing elected with 50.81% of votes cast (19 May 1974)

debat-1981.title: 1981: the 1974 rematch
debat-1981.text: On 5 May 1981 the 1974 rivals met again, Giscard d'Estaing now as outgoing president. Mitterrand's team set 21 conditions (set, filming, journalists' role). Giscard contrasted his record of running France with what he called Mitterrand's 'ministry of words'.
debat-1981.why: It shows that the debate's format (set, cameras, journalists) is negotiated between the candidates, a practice that continues today.
debat-1981.quote: It is rather awkward that in the meantime you have become, yourself, the man of the deficit.
debat-1981.result: François Mitterrand elected with 51.76% of votes cast (10 May 1981)

debat-1988.title: 1988: the president versus his prime minister
debat-1988.text: On 28 April 1988, after two years of 'cohabitation', President Mitterrand faced his prime minister, Jacques Chirac. Chirac asked to call him 'Mr Mitterrand'; Mitterrand replied: 'But you are quite right, Mr Prime Minister.'
debat-1988.why: The only runoff debate between a sitting president and his own prime minister: it shows the tensions of 'cohabitation' at the top of the state.
debat-1988.quote: Tonight, I am not the prime minister, and you are not the president of the Republic.
debat-1988.result: François Mitterrand re-elected with 54.02% of votes cast (8 May 1988)

debat-1995.title: 1995: a courteous debate and the five-year term
debat-1995.text: On 2 May 1995, Jacques Chirac (RPR) and Lionel Jospin (PS) held a courteous debate moderated by Alain Duhamel and Guillaume Durand. Jospin argued for a five-year presidential term instead of seven; his quip made Chirac laugh.
debat-1995.why: The five-year term raised that night was adopted by referendum on 24 September 2000 (over 73% yes).
debat-1995.quote: Better five years with Jospin than seven years with Chirac.
debat-1995.result: Jacques Chirac elected with 52.64% of votes cast (7 May 1995)

debat-2002.title: 2002: the debate that never happened
debat-2002.text: On 21 April 2002, Jean-Marie Le Pen (FN) reaches the second round against the outgoing president Jacques Chirac. On 23 April, in Rennes, Chirac announces he refuses to debate him.
debat-2002.why: The only presidential election without a runoff debate since 1974: the debate is a tradition, not a legal requirement.
debat-2002.quote: I cannot accept the normalisation of intolerance and hatred.
debat-2002.result: Jacques Chirac re-elected with 82.21% of votes cast (5 May 2002)

debat-2007.title: 2007: 'Calm down' and anger owned
debat-2007.text: On 2 May 2007, Nicolas Sarkozy (UMP) and Ségolène Royal (PS) debated for 2 h 40 on TF1 and France 2. On schooling for disabled children, Royal said she was 'very angry'; Sarkozy replied: 'To be president of the Republic, you have to be calm.'
debat-2007.why: The first debate between the two rounds with a woman candidate.
debat-2007.result: Nicolas Sarkozy elected with 53.06% of votes cast (6 May 2007)

debat-2012.title: 2012: the 'Me, as president' refrain
debat-2012.text: On 2 May 2012, outgoing president Nicolas Sarkozy (UMP) faced François Hollande (PS), with Laurence Ferrari and David Pujadas moderating. Asked what president he would be, Hollande answered with a long series of sentences opening 'Me, as president…'.
debat-2012.why: The line stuck: promises made during the debate are later quoted back during the term, as in a written question in the Assemblée as early as 2014.
debat-2012.quote: As president of the Republic, I will not be the head of the majority…
debat-2012.result: François Hollande elected with 51.64% of votes cast (6 May 2012)

debat-2017.title: 2017: a very heated debate
debat-2017.text: On 3 May 2017, Emmanuel Macron (En Marche!) and Marine Le Pen (FN) clashed in a very heated debate watched by 16.5 million viewers. The euro, Europe, terrorism: attacks came from both sides; Macron called her proposals 'snake oil' ('poudre de perlimpinpin').
debat-2017.why: The first debate between the two rounds with a far-right candidate, after the refusal to debate in 2002.
debat-2017.quote: Either way, France will be led by a woman: it will be either me or Mrs Merkel.
debat-2017.result: Emmanuel Macron elected with 66.10% of votes cast (7 May 2017)

debat-2022.title: 2022: the rematch
debat-2022.text: On 20 April 2022, outgoing president Emmanuel Macron and Marine Le Pen (RN) met again for nearly 3 hours, hosted by Léa Salamé and Gilles Bouleau. Cost of living, Europe, Russia, climate: on the Russian loan, Le Pen replied 'We are a poor party'.
debat-2022.why: The second rematch after 1974–1981: held during the war in Ukraine, it shows how world events enter the debate.
debat-2022.quote: You are speaking to your banker when you speak about Russia.
debat-2022.result: Emmanuel Macron re-elected with 58.55% of votes cast (24 April 2022)

melenchon-1986-senat.title: Elected senator for Essonne
melenchon-1986-senat.text: Elected senator for Essonne on 28 September 1986, re-elected in 1995 and 2004. His term ended in January 2010 after his election to the European Parliament.

melenchon-2000-ministre.title: Minister for Vocational Education
melenchon-2000-ministre.text: Appointed Minister Delegate for Vocational Education, attached to the Minister of National Education, in Lionel Jospin's government (2000-2002).

melenchon-2012-presidentielle.title: 2012 presidential election: 11.10%
melenchon-2012-presidentielle.text: Running for president, he received 3,984,822 votes in the first round, i.e. 11.10% of valid votes (4th place).

melenchon-2017-presidentielle.title: 2017 presidential election: 19.58%
melenchon-2017-presidentielle.text: Running for president, he received 7,059,951 votes in the first round, i.e. 19.58% of valid votes (4th place).

melenchon-2022-presidentielle.title: 2022 presidential election: 21.95%
melenchon-2022-presidentielle.text: Running for president, he received 7,712,520 votes in the first round, i.e. 21.95% of valid votes (3rd place).

melenchon-2027-candidature.title: Declared candidate for 2027
melenchon-2027-candidature.text: On 3 May 2026, on TF1's 8 pm news, he announced he is running in the 2027 presidential election.

roussel-2017-depute.title: Elected MP for the Nord
roussel-2017-depute.text: Elected MP for the Nord's 20th constituency on 18 June 2017, he was re-elected in 2022. His term ended on 9 June 2024.

roussel-2018-pcf.title: National secretary of the PCF
roussel-2018-pcf.text: Elected head of the French Communist Party at the Ivry-sur-Seine congress, succeeding Pierre Laurent as national secretary.

roussel-2022-presidentielle.title: 2022 presidential election: 2.28%
roussel-2022-presidentielle.text: Running for president, he received 802,422 votes in the first round, i.e. 2.28% of valid votes.

roussel-2026-maire.title: Re-elected mayor of Saint-Amand-les-Eaux
roussel-2026-maire.text: Mayor of Saint-Amand-les-Eaux (Nord) since 2025, he was re-elected in the first round of the municipal elections, his list winning 51.06% of the vote.

roussel-2027-candidature.title: PCF candidate for 2027
roussel-2027-candidature.text: On 6 September 2026, PCF members approved his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election with 72% of the vote.

glucksmann-2018-place-publique.title: Co-founds Place publique
glucksmann-2018-place-publique.text: With about twenty civil-society figures, he launched a new party, Place publique.

glucksmann-2019-depute-europeen.title: Member of the European Parliament
glucksmann-2019-depute-europeen.text: Elected in the 2019 European elections, he has sat in the European Parliament since 2 July 2019, in the Socialists and Democrats (S&D) group.

glucksmann-2020-inge.title: Chair of a European Parliament special committee
glucksmann-2020-inge.text: He was elected chair of the European Parliament's special committee on foreign interference in democratic processes (INGE).

glucksmann-2024-europeennes.title: 2024 European elections: 13.83%
glucksmann-2024-europeennes.text: Leading the PS–Place publique list in the European elections, his list won 13.83% of the vote (3rd place).

glucksmann-2026-candidature.title: Announces his candidacy
glucksmann-2026-candidature.text: On 23 August 2026, he announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election and his participation in a social-democratic left primary.

glucksmann-2026-primaire.title: Chosen by the social-democratic primary
glucksmann-2026-primaire.text: He won the social-democratic left primary in the first round (vote held 9-11 October 2026) with over 66% of the vote, becoming its 2027 candidate.

attal-2017-depute.title: Elected MP for Hauts-de-Seine
attal-2017-depute.text: Elected MP for the 10th constituency of Hauts-de-Seine on 18 June 2017. He was re-elected in 2022 and 2024.

attal-2018-gouvernement.title: Joins the government
attal-2018-gouvernement.text: Appointed Secretary of State to the Minister of National Education and Youth in Édouard Philippe's government.

attal-2024-premier-ministre.title: Prime Minister
attal-2024-premier-ministre.text: The President of the Republic appointed him Prime Minister on 9 January 2024 and asked him to form a government.

attal-2024-renaissance.title: Secretary-general of Renaissance
attal-2024-renaissance.text: He was elected secretary-general of the Renaissance party with 94.9% of the vote.

attal-2027-candidature.title: Declared candidate for 2027
attal-2027-candidature.text: On 22 May 2026, he announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election during a visit to Aveyron.

philippe-2010-maire.title: Mayor of Le Havre
philippe-2010-maire.text: He succeeded Antoine Rufenacht as mayor of Le Havre (Seine-Maritime).

philippe-2012-depute.title: MP for Seine-Maritime
philippe-2012-depute.text: He became MP for the 7th constituency of Seine-Maritime in March 2012 and was re-elected in June 2012. He left the Assembly in 2017 on joining the government.

philippe-2017-premier-ministre.title: Prime Minister
philippe-2017-premier-ministre.text: Emmanuel Macron appointed him Prime Minister on 15 May 2017.

philippe-2021-horizons.title: Founds the Horizons party
philippe-2021-horizons.text: Fifteen months after leaving Matignon, he launched his own party, Horizons, in Le Havre.

philippe-2024-candidature.title: Announces his candidacy
philippe-2024-candidature.text: In an interview with Le Point published on 3 September 2024, he announced he would run in the next presidential election.

philippe-2026-maire.title: Re-elected mayor of Le Havre
philippe-2026-maire.text: He was re-elected mayor of Le Havre in the municipal run-off with about 47% of the vote. He had presented this re-election as a step before his 2027 candidacy.

retailleau-2004-senat.title: Elected senator for Vendée
retailleau-2004-senat.text: Elected senator for Vendée on 26 September 2004, he was re-elected in 2014, 2020 and 2026.

retailleau-2014-groupe-senat.title: Leader of the UMP, then LR, group in the Senate
retailleau-2014-groupe-senat.text: He became leader of the UMP (later LR) group in the Senate, a post he held for ten years until joining the government in 2024.

retailleau-2024-interieur.title: Minister of the Interior
retailleau-2024-interieur.text: He was appointed Minister of the Interior in Michel Barnier's government.

retailleau-2025-president-lr.title: President of Les Républicains
retailleau-2025-president-lr.text: He was elected president of Les Républicains by party members with 74.31% of the vote, against Laurent Wauquiez.

retailleau-2027-candidature.title: Chosen as LR candidate for 2027
retailleau-2027-candidature.text: In an internal vote, Les Républicains members chose to designate him directly as their 2027 presidential candidate, with 73.8% of the vote.

wauquiez-2004-depute.title: Elected MP for Haute-Loire
wauquiez-2004-depute.text: He was elected UMP MP for Haute-Loire in the first round. He was re-elected in 2007 and 2012.

wauquiez-2011-ministre.title: Minister of Higher Education
wauquiez-2011-ministre.text: He was appointed Minister of Higher Education and Research in François Fillon's government.

wauquiez-2016-region.title: President of the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region
wauquiez-2016-region.text: He became president of the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes regional council and stepped down as mayor of Le Puy-en-Velay, which he had led since 2008.

wauquiez-2017-president-lr.title: President of Les Républicains
wauquiez-2017-president-lr.text: He was elected president of Les Républicains in the first round with 74.64% of the vote.

wauquiez-2024-groupe-an.title: Leader of the Droite républicaine group
wauquiez-2024-groupe-an.text: Re-elected MP for Haute-Loire in July 2024, he became leader of the Droite républicaine group in the National Assembly.

wauquiez-2026-position.title: Position on 2027
wauquiez-2026-position.text: On 1 July 2026, he said Édouard Philippe "can embody order and seriousness" and called for a single candidate of the right and centre.

lepen-1998-region.title: First office: regional councillor
lepen-1998-region.text: She was first elected in 1998, as a regional councillor in Nord-Pas-de-Calais. She later served as an MEP (2004-2017) and as MP for Pas-de-Calais (since 2017).

lepen-2011-presidente-fn.title: President of the Front national
lepen-2011-presidente-fn.text: She succeeded her father, Jean-Marie Le Pen, as leader of the Front national (now Rassemblement national).

lepen-2012-presidentielle.title: 2012 presidential election: 17.90%
lepen-2012-presidentielle.text: Running for president, she received 6,421,426 votes in the first round, i.e. 17.90% of valid votes (3rd place).

lepen-2017-presidentielle.title: 2017 presidential election: 21.30%
lepen-2017-presidentielle.text: She received 7,678,491 votes in the first round, i.e. 21.30% of valid votes (2nd place), qualifying for the run-off against Emmanuel Macron.

lepen-2022-presidentielle.title: 2022 presidential election: 23.15%
lepen-2022-presidentielle.text: She received 8,133,828 votes in the first round, i.e. 23.15% of valid votes (2nd place), qualifying for the run-off against Emmanuel Macron.

lepen-2026-appel-candidature.title: Appeal ruling and candidacy
lepen-2026-appel-candidature.text: On 7 July 2026, the Paris Court of Appeal sentenced her notably to 45 months' ineligibility, 30 of them suspended, so she can run. She declared her candidacy and appealed to the Court of Cassation.

bardella-2015-region.title: First office: regional councillor
bardella-2015-region.text: He was elected regional councillor for Île-de-France, his first elected office, at the age of 20. He left this seat in February 2025.

bardella-2019-depute-europeen.title: Member of the European Parliament
bardella-2019-depute-europeen.text: Elected in the 2019 European elections on the Rassemblement national list, he has sat in the European Parliament since 2 July 2019.

bardella-2022-president-rn.title: President of the Rassemblement national
bardella-2022-president-rn.text: He was elected president of the Rassemblement national at the party congress in Paris, against Louis Aliot, succeeding Marine Le Pen.

bardella-2024-europeennes.title: 2024 European elections: 31.37%
bardella-2024-europeennes.text: Leading the Rassemblement national list in the European elections, his list came first with 31.37% of the vote.

bardella-2026-statut.title: Status for 2027
bardella-2026-statut.text: After the 7 July 2026 appeal ruling, Marine Le Pen is the RN candidate. He is not running: he is presented as her Prime Minister if she wins.

zemmour-2021-candidature.title: Enters politics: presidential bid
zemmour-2021-candidature.text: He announced his candidacy for the 2022 presidential election in a video posted on social media.

zemmour-2021-reconquete.title: Founds the Reconquête party
zemmour-2021-reconquete.text: At a rally in Villepinte, he launched his campaign and his party, Reconquête.

zemmour-2022-presidentielle.title: 2022 presidential election: 7.07%
zemmour-2022-presidentielle.text: Running for president, he received 2,485,226 votes in the first round, i.e. 7.07% of valid votes (4th place).

zemmour-2022-legislatives.title: Parliamentary candidate in the Var
zemmour-2022-legislatives.text: Running in the parliamentary elections in the Var's 4th constituency, he did not qualify for the run-off.

zemmour-2027-candidature.title: Declared candidate for 2027
zemmour-2027-candidature.text: On 17 September 2026, on BFMTV, the Reconquête president confirmed his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election.

registered.question: Are you on the electoral roll?
registered.help: To vote in the presidential election, you must be registered by Friday 12 March 2027 at the latest.

knowledge.question: The President of the Republic is elected for…
knowledge.explanation: Since 2002, the presidential term has lasted 5 years (the quinquennat).

knowledge.question: Who votes on laws in France?
knowledge.explanation: Laws are voted by Parliament: the Assemblée nationale (National Assembly) and the Senate.

knowledge.question: How many députés (MPs) are there in the Assemblée nationale?
knowledge.explanation: There are 577 députés. 348 is the number of senators.

debutant.label: Beginner
debutant.text: We start with the basics, then the campaign news, explained simply.

intermediaire.label: Intermediate
intermediaire.text: A reminder of the key rules, then news from all sides.

avance.label: Advanced
avance.text: Straight to the campaign news, from all sides.

ideas.question: Your position (optional)
ideas.privacy: It stays only on your phone. We only use it to show you the other sides' ideas more often. We will never tell you who to vote for.

voter.question: Can you vote in the French presidential election?

options.label: No, I'm from a non-EU country

help.eu: You don't vote in the presidential election, but you can vote in municipal and European elections in France.
help.non-eu: You don't vote in political elections in France, but the presidential election can change your life here: visas, studies, jobs. We adapt your feed.
help.nsp: No problem: we explain who can vote in your feed.

tutorial.title: Read the news
tutorial.text: Short, sourced cards from all sides. Swipe up or use the arrows.

tutorial.title: Play
tutorial.text: After 3 cards, a quick challenge. Every right answer earns you voix (the game's points), and we always explain the right answer.

tutorial.title: Grow your town and challenge your friends
tutorial.text: Your voix build your town. Send a challenge to a friend: they play the same questions and you compare.
